Commentary.Commentary: It was Keshav Maharaj who backed them up, taking two vital wickets to dismiss Ben Stokes and Jonny Bairstow. Chris Morris then turned around his bad day taking three quick wickets to run through the England tail. They will be delighted with the 130-run lead. They will want to get a good score in since batting will get tougher on this wicket which is misbehaving. England have to play catch-up from here, let's see how they go. Can they trigger a collapse? Joe Root will hope for that. Join us to see how they go with the ball now.

A fine, fine performance from South Africa. When they were bundled out early today it looked like the hosts would dominate the proceedings. They came out firing and took out the openers in a jiffy. Joe Root put in an amazing batting performance to stroke his way to 78. England were right on top at the lunch break but South Africa came roaring back in the game with wickets after that. Senior men, Vernon Philander and Morne Morkel took the big wickets of Gary Ballance and Joe Root and set it up for the them.

OUT! Very good catch, Faf! Short from Morris in line of the body of the batsman, Wood just fends at it from his body. The ball flies to the right of Faf du Plessis at second slip. He takes it really well leaping to his right. A very good catch to end the day. ENGLAND BOWLED OUT FOR 205.
Shorter and on the body, Wood arches back and gets out of the way dropping his wrists.
Short and outside off, Wood looks to ramp it over the keeper but misses.
FOUR! Handy hit! Shorter in length outside off, Wood pulls it hard through mid-wicket for a boundary. That was nicely pulled.
Full and outside off, Wood drives it towards mid off.
Floats it wide outside off, turns in, Anderson is happy to let it go.
Tossed up around off, clipped through mid on for a single.
Tries to slide the arm ball around off, Wood is happy to block it.
Wood lunges forward and pushes it back down the wicket.
Too full from Maharaj, Wood blocks it.
Floats it outside off, Wood comes forward and pushes it towards covers.
Fuller outside off, Anderson looks to keep it out but gets an inside edge onto his pads.
Short in length, Wood gets off the mark with a nudge wide of the short leg fielder. 200 up for England.
Back of a length outside off, Wood punches it towards point. There is a bit of a fumble but they don't take the single.
Shorter in length on middle, Wood thinks to pull but then aborts his shot.
Slants this on the pads, Wood looks to clip but the ball keeps low and hits him on the pads.
Shorter in length on the stumps, Wood fends it towards short leg.
Lands it outside off, Anderson comes forward to defend but fails to connect. The short leg fielder takes the catch but no harm done as there was no bat there.
Anderson looks to reverse sweep but gets it straight onto the legs of the keeper.
Lands it around off, James stays back and punches it towards the leg side.
Shorter outside off, Anderson punches it back to the bowler.
Jimmy Anderson is the last man in.

OUT! Another one bites the dust! Maharaj keeps it around off, Dawson wants to sweep it. The ball goes off the top edge and Hashim Amla gets under it at backward square leg. A safe catch. England are going down rather quickly here. Third wicket for Keshav Maharaj. England still trail by 136 runs. First time since 2007 that a spinner has taken more than 2 wickets at Trent Bridge in the first innings.
Floats it around off, Dawson comes forward to defend and does so well.
Shorter in length, Wood shapes to defend but gets it off the handle of the bat towards the off side. Double-wicket maiden for Chris Morris.
Banged in short but way outside off, Wood is happy to stay away from it.
Shorter length ball outside off, Wood drops his wrists and lets it go.
Goes for the full one on the stumps, Wood is up to it and defends it back down the wicket. Well thought out that since Wood might have been expecting a short one.
Mark Wood is the new man in. He'll have to deal with the hat-trick ball. Three slips, leg gully and a short leg greet him.

OUT! Two in two, South Africa on top! Full and spearing into the stumps, Broad is late on this and is hit on his pads. The players appeal for an lbw but the umpire says no. If Broad has not hit that, could be close. Replays show there was no bat there. Hawk Eye shows three reds and that is another wicket for Morris. Golden duck for Broad, even he was waiting for the short one and had his weight back. Two in two for Chris and he is on a hat-trick.
South Africa have taken a review for lbw. Unless he has hit this, it could be close.
Stuart Broad comes out to bat. He will play his shots.

OUT! Morris strikes! Ali waiting for the short one but gets a fuller one outside off, slices it straight to cover-point. Faf du Plessis takes the catch and that is a wicket gifted but is it one earned as well? There was a field change before this delivery, the plan was to push him back and get him pushing at fuller ones. Difference between Elgar and Faf? He and Morris look absolutely pumped up and why not. England still trail by 136 runs. So du Plessis came in from second slip and moved himself to that position and it worked immediately.
Floats it around off, pushed towards mid off by Liam.
FOUR! Poor ball, hit away! Slides this down the leg side, Dawson does not miss out and sweeps it down to the fine leg fence. Maharaj turned around the moment he saw that he had bowled it down leg.
Spots Dawson coming down, shortens his length, Liam turns it towards the leg side.
Another forward block by Dawson.
Lands it outside off, Dawson comes forward and defends it.
Shorter around off, Dawson camps back to cut but finds the fielder at point.
Full and outside off, Ali drives it hard and crashes it through covers. Kuhn gets to his left from sweeper cover and stops it from going through. A couple taken.
Gets in line of this one and defends it towards the leg side from his crease.
Shorter and this time on middle and leg, Ali just lets it pass over him.
Slants it on a similar length around off, Ali gets out of the way easily.
South Africa have two men back for the hook.
Shorter and outside off, Moeen thinks about playing a shot but spots that it is too wide and lets it go.
Shorter outside off, Moeen stays back and punches it towards covers.
Dawson is right forward to defend it.
Angles it around middle and off, Dawson lunges forward and defends it.
Spots Ali coming down, floats it around off. Moeen whips it through mid-wicket for a single.
Tossed up outside off, Ali looks to get forward and turn it through the leg side but is hit on his pad off the spin. Can't give it out since it was way outside off.
Loops it outside off, Ali comes forward to defend but does off the inner half.
Lands it outside off, spins in a touch, Ali stays back and defends it.
Shorter in length on middle, worked through backward square leg for a couple of runs. He has been a wayward right from the start.
Back of a length just around off, Dawson stands tall and punches it towards covers.
Full and outside off, Dawson shapes to drive but is beaten all ends up. He needs to bowl more of these.
England have scored 25 percent of their runs through third man. That's a lot, isn't it?
Wasted delivery down the leg side on a shorter length, Dawson ducks under it.
FOUR! Edged! Outside off on a good length, Dawson looks to defend but the ball goes off the outside edge down to the third man fence for a boundary.

NOT OUT! Good review! Morris bowls it outside off, Dawson looks to punch it through but seems to have edged it. The keeper collects and appeals. The umpire rules it out. Dawson goes for the review instantly. Replays show why, there was daylight between bat and ball there. Wonder what made the umpire give it out. Morris was almost celebrating without appealing. Shudder to think if there were no reviews.......
Dawson is given out caught behind. He has reviewed it though.
Chris Morris to bowl from the other end. He has to step up and perform. He has a word of advice from Morkel.
Bowls it outside off, Ali is watchful as he comes forward and defends it back down the wicket.
Punches this one towards point and takes a quick single.
Tossed up outside off, pushed to covers by Liam coming forward.
Floats it around the stumps, Dawson lunges forward and keeps it out.
Around off again, Dawson comes forward and defends it.
Lands it around off, Ali clips it through mid-wicket for a single.

The players are out for the final session. Moeen Ali and Liam Dawson come out to bat. Will they play their shots or take their time? Let's see. Keshav Maharaj to start things off in the final session. He has an in-out field.
... Day 2, Session 3...

Despite pocketing the session, the Proteas' think tank would be worrying over the support seamers Olivier and Morris. The latter only bowled an over in the session but both of them have been unimpressive so far. The senior men, Philander in particular, have been brilliant while Maharaj has also proven to be more than a handful with the footholes. An interesting final session beckons, one that could possibly decide which way this game is heading. Join us shortly for the post-tea phase.

Excellent session for South Africa. They needed it after the Root-Ballance partnership that was flourishing. Philander struck in his first over after lunch to remove the southpaw but Root seemed to be chugging along to another century with Bairstow for company. Morkel, bowling an extended spell, then delivered a big blow to send the England captain on his way back. Keshav Maharaj struck two deadly blows thereafter, removing Stokes and Bairstow rather quickly to push the advantage firmly in favor of the visitors.
Back of a length angled in around off stump, defended solidly from the crease towards the off side. TEA ON DAY 2.
Fullish on the pads, worked away to deep mid-wicket for a single.
On a shortish length outside off, Ali thinks about playing at it but withdraws the bat eventually.
Shane Warne wants South Africa to go short and quick on the body. Ali has been susceptible to the short stuff at times.

Short of a length outside off, punched off the back foot through the covers. A brace to the total. Morris has been dismal so far, he needs to redeem himself if South Africa are to do well as Philander and Morkel cannot do all the work.
Sprayed down the leg side, easy pickings for Dawson who clips it to deep square leg for a single.
Shortish on leg stump, Ali rises on his toes to tuck it through backward square leg for a single.
Chris Morris comes on for a bowl. Can he strike at the stroke of Tea?
Tossed up nicely around off, defended firmly off the front foot.
Fullish around middle and leg, Dawson leans across and pushes it to the left of the short leg fielder.
Slightly shorter outside off, punched off the back foot towards long on for a single.
Short leg is in place now.
Tossed up outside off, turns in from the footholes as Ali looks to push at it. Gets an inside edge towards short fine leg.
Flighted around off, driven towards the extra cover region as the mid off fielder gets across to his left to stop it. Single taken, relief for Dawson after the pair at Lord's.
Liam Dawson comes out to bat. England will want the lower order to come good here.

OUT! GOT HIM! That's a left-arm spinner's delight, what a peach! Tossed up around middle, draws Bairstow forward and he is beaten by the turn as the ball crashes into the off stump. Massive, massive wicket this for South Africa. They are chipping away nicely and it's Maharaj who has proven to be the surprise package on a day where the seamers have been dominating. Two big wickets for him, both with excellent deliveries.
On a shortish length outside off, Moeen sits back and defends it to the off side.

FOUR! Nicely stroked! Back of a length outside off, Ali stands tall and essays a beautiful back foot punch through extra cover. Elegant stroke and the ball races to the fence for a boundary. That was so soothing to the eyes.
Just full and on fourth stump line, Ali doesn't offer a stroke to that one.
Fullish ball outside off, crisply driven by Moeen towards the extra cover fielder.
Erratic from Philander, sprayed way outside off as Ali makes an easy leave.
On a length wider outside off, left alone to the keeper.
Low full toss outside off, driven fluently towards the man at mid off.
The slider around middle, JB gets his bat down in time and defends solidly.
Flatter outside off, stays back and defends it towards cover.
Floated outside off, reaches out to that one and taps it towards cover.
Flatter around off, Bairstow leans into it to block but gets a thick inside edge on to the pads.
Flighted around off, wristed in front of square on the leg side for a single.
Length ball closer to off stump, Bairstow plays late with an angled bat. Steered on the bounce towards the gully fielder.
On a shortish length around off stump, defended off the back foot towards point.
Beaten! That's a lovely delivery from Philander! Length ball on fourth stump line, shapes away a shade as Bairstow is beaten on the poke.
Back of a length just outside off, stays back and stabs it to the off side.
Fullish on middle stump line, JB gets across and pushes it towards mid on.
Philander gets nice away shape on this length ball pitched just outside off, late movement and Bairstow smartly lets it pass.
Flatter outside off, Ali sits back and punches it towards the on side.
Flighted nicely outside off, Ali looks to push at it but gets an inside edge on to the pads.
Deepish mid-wicket in place.
FOUR! BANG! What a shot to play first ball! Confidence personified! Tossed up just outside off, Ali gets across on one leg and slogs it over mid-wicket. Clean strike and it runs away to the fence.
In walks the hero of the last game, Moeen Ali. He has a job to do here. A short leg in place.

OUT! MAHARAJ STRIKES! Another big wicket for South Africa! Looped up nicely outside off, turns in a touch with extra bounce as Stokes prods forward to defend. Gets a faint inside edge that strikes his pads and bobbles up to hit de Kock on his shoulder off his glove. The SA keeper reacts in time to take it eventually on the rebound. The umpires want to check if the ball struck Quinton's grill and the third umpire is convinced that it hasn't. So, Stokes has to continue walking to the dressing room, it's a duck for him. The visitors will be glad as the southpaw can turn a game around in no time. Probably the starvation of strike in this partnership undid his concentration a bit although the delivery was a good one.
Is that out? Ben Stokes seems to have been caught off the inside edge. The umpires are checking if the ball hit the grill of the helmet of the keeper in the process of the catch.
Square leg goes fine now.
Flighted outside off, reaches out and taps it gently to the off side.
Floated outside off, Stokes presses forward and blocks it solidly towards cover.
Length ball around off stump, defended from the crease to the off side.
Dean Elgar takes the ball to the umpire complaining about the shape. The umpire finds it good enough and hands it back to Elgar.

FOUR! Chipped over the bowler's head! Nicely done by Bairstow, leans forward to this fuller ball and extends his forward defence a bit to get the elevation. Lofts it very straight and it runs away to the fence for a boundary.
Good length angled in around off stump, Bairstow gets behind the line nicely and defends towards cover.
On a length around the fourth stump line, jags away as Bairstow lets it pass.

Cracker from Philander! His misfields will be forgiven if he can nip a few wickets here. This is on a length around off stump, shapes away sharply to beat the outside edge as Jonny is beaten on the poke.
Length ball outside off, punched sweetly towards the mid off fielder.
Philander messes up again! Second time now that he has gifted runs. Flatter outside off, punched towards backward point where Vernon is late to get down. Lets it through as the batsmen get a run.
Fired in on leg stump, Bairstow sweeps well but there is a man at short backward square leg. Straight to him, so another dot ball.
Flighted on off stump, nicely defended back to the bowler by Bairstow.
Slows it down around middle, Bairstow gets the front foot nicely forward and smothers it to the ground.
The slider outside off, JB gets half forward and defends strongly to cover.
Fuller outside off, leans forward and drives it towards mid off.
Time for some spin. Keshav Maharaj comes back on for a bowl.

More streaky runs for Bairstow! He's nearing a fifty but is yet to look assured at the crease. Length ball outside off, loose drive from JB as the ball goes off the outer half through backward point. The gully fielder chases it down and saves a run for his side. Bavuma at point slipped twice trying to stop that one.
Shortish outside off, nips in a bit as JB looks to push at it. The inside edge raps him on the pads.
Back of a length outside off, punched off the back foot towards cover.

NOT OUT! There was a faint edge and that saves Bairstow. On a length around middle, shapes away late to rap Jonny on the pads. Huge appeal for lbw, turned down by the umpire. Philander is confident and du Plessis doesn't waste time to take the review. Height could be the only factor here, or so we assume but the Snicko has a twist to offer. There is a slight spike which means a faint edge on it. That settles the case then, South Africa lose a review.
South Africa have reviewed a lbw call against Bairstow. The Proteas are confident, Philander in particular. Only height could be the issue perhaps.
On a shortish length outside off, keeps a bit low as Bairstow adjusts to punch it towards cover.
Back of a length outside off, left alone to the keeper.
Vernon Philander returns for a burst.  South Africa have to do that, to not let England feel at home with the scoring.
Leg bye! Fullish on leg stump, Bairstow misses the flick and the ball goes off the pads towards the leg side. The batsmen sneak a leg bye.

FOUR! Fab stroke! That should ease him back into the flow! Length ball outside off, Bairstow unfurls a lovely drive through extra cover. Beautifully timed and Kuhn from sweeper cover makes a valiant attempt to his left, putting in a desperate dive as well but couldn't prevent the boundary.
Fullish on off stump, swinging in a bit as the ball goes off the inner half of Bairstow's blade to mid-wicket. A slightly nervy phase at the moment for Jonny although he has got the luck going.

FOUR! Sloppy from Philander! He should have stopped that. Fuller outside off, Bairstow dishes out a punchy drive towards mid off where Vernon mistimes his slide and lets it through to the fence. South Africa shouldn't be gifting away runs like this.
Fuller this time on off stump, reaches out and drives it back to the bowler.
Back of a length around off, punched firmly back to the bowler.
Short of a good length around off, darting in as Bairstow jabs it towards square leg for a single.
Length ball around middle, gets across and tucks it towards the leg side.
Short of a good length outside off, punchy drive from JB towards cover.
Fullish on middle, crisply driven by Bairstow but straight towards mid on.

Off the inner half now! Bairstow is having the rub of the green going his way. Back of a length around off stump, nips in sharply as the ball flies off the inside edge just past leg stump as it goes to fine leg. Brace taken.
Two gullies in place now.

FOUR! Off the edge but in the gap! Bairstow gets lucky, he surely wasn't in control there. Back of a length ball outside off, Jonny pushes away from the body and gets a thick edge that flies wide of the gully fielder. Boundary to third man.
Length ball around middle, gets across and clips it to the leg side.
On a length around middle, Stokes shuffles a touch and taps it to the left of the mid on fielder.
Fullish around middle, a hint of inswing as Stokes pushes gently towards mid on.
Bouncer from Olivier on off stump, Stokes ducks under the high bumper.
Back of a length around middle, stays back and whips it behind square on the leg side for a single.
Good length around middle, a bit of extra bounce as Bairstow taps it down the pitch off the bat sticker.
On a good length closer to off stump, straightens after pitching, good leave by Stokes.
Just fractionally short of a good length outside off, Stokes doesn't offer a stroke to that one.

Gets his length fuller this time outside off, blocked firmly off the front foot towards cover. This should be a riveting bout - Stokes vs Morkel, provided the tall pacer is kept on for few more overs.
Another bumper but this time down the leg side, easier for Stokes to negotiate this time as he gets out of the way.
Short ball around off stump, Stokes arches his back to evade the bumper.
Ben Stokes comes out to bat. He has not got going in this series so far and will be itching to perform.

Drinks break taken. That wicket just at the stroke of the mini break will boost South Africa. They needed that badly. Even-stevens at the moment. Joe Root alone has scored 78 runs and the rest combined today have scored only 91 runs for seven wickets. Shows the class of the batsman, doesn't it?

OUT! That is a big, big, big wicket! Morkel bowls it outside off on a good length, shapes away, Root thinks he can drive it away but gets an outside edge. The ball flies to the right of de Kock who dives and takes the catch. You live by the sword, you die by it. That is a huge wicket in context of this game. He was the one who was taking the attack to the opposition and now South Africa have broken through just in time. England trail by 192 runs.
Good length outside off, Bairstow mistimes his punch towards covers.
WIDE! Sprays it way outside off, Bairstow cannot reach it.
Bairstow comes forward and defends it.
Played to point by the batsman. He is playing his shots at the moment.
Lands it outside off, left alone.
Bairstow tickles one towards fine leg from his crease. The fielder does well to stop the ball near the fence. Two runs taken.
Good length outside off, Root taps it towards point for a single.
Four Byes! Lands it outside off, Bairstow looks to defend but the ball swings in and beats the keeper diving to his left. Boundary results.
Turns it towards mid-wicket from his crease.
On a length, pushed towards mid off.
Wide outside off, no shot offered by the batsman.
Good length outside off, Root taps it towards point and takes a single.
FOUR! Poor ball! Shorter in length around middle, pulled down to fine leg for a boundary by Root. He continues to motor along.
Wide enough for a leave by Bairstow.
FOUR! Top shot! Stand and deliver! Length outside off, Bairstow comes forward and spanks it through covers for a boundary.
Full around off, Bairstow looks to drive but gets it off the outer half through covers. Bavuma goes after it from covers and stops the ball. Cannot prevent the two though.
Angles it around middle, Bairstow clips it through mid-wicket for a couple of runs. Olivier is going too straight at the moment.
Good length outside off, left alone by Bairstow.
Full outside off, Root comes forward and drives it to point.
Duanne Olivier comes on for a burst.
Full and outside off, left alone by the batsman.
Ian Botham feels that South Africa's score is above average for this wicket. England will feel that too but South Africa have to bowl well to maintain the pressure.
Length ball outside off, Bairstow looks to punch it on the up but misses. That came in a long way.
Root taps it to backward point and takes a quick single.

Short again, this time Root plays a controlled pull through square leg. Maharaj comes across from long leg and slides to stop the ball. Philander gets to his right to help him out, the spinner fumbles but still only two runs taken.
FOUR! Edged! Back of a length outside off, Root runs it down past the gully fielder for a boundary. The runs are flowing off his bat today. South Africa haven't bowled that well to him.
Ouch! Back of a length around off, Root shapes to pull but this one does not bounce much and is hit on his body. He is all smiles though.
Good length outside off, played towards deep point for a single.
FOUR! Poor ball and punished! A tad short outside off, Root picks it early and pulls it nicely through mid-wicket for a boundary. That raced away to the fence.
Full around off, Joe comes forward and taps it to covers.
Slants it on the pads, Bairstow cannot clip it. The ball rolls wide of the keeper and they take a leg bye.
Full and wide outside off, pushed to deep point for a single.
Fuller outside off, Root drives it nicely towards mid off. There is a direct hit at the bowler's end and Root wants the run but is sent back.
Around off on a length, a solid defence from Bairstow keeps it out.
Width from Morkel, Root slaps it to deep point for a single.
Fuller outside off, Root drives it back to the bowler.
Gets behind the line of this one and defends it back down the wicket.
Outside off on a good length, left alone.
Duanne Olivier is warming up. Important for them to back up their experienced bowlers.
Root stays in his crease and defends this one from his crease.
The beehive for Morkel and Philander shows that the latter has made the batsmen play more bowling closer to the stumps.
Length around off, Bairstow turns it towards mid-wicket again.
Good length around off, Bairstow turns it towards mid-wicket from his crease.
Punches this one through the off side for a single.
How dearly would Faf have wanted Rabada here? His back up bowlers in Chris Morris and Duanne Olivier have not hit their mark. Rabada would have enjoyed bowling here.
Around off, Root stays back and defends it back down the wicket.
Slants it on the pads, turned through mid-wicket for a brace. Root has looked in control right from the start.
Full and outside off, swings further away, Root lets it go through.
Bring this one into the batsman from outside off, Bairstow looks to play through the off side but is beaten by the inward movement.

FOUR! Educated edge! Outside off on a good length, Bairstow angles it wide of the gully fielder for a boundary to third man. England batsmen will play their shots, so that keeps the South African bowlers in the game all the while.
Good length outside off, Bairstow stays in his crease and defends it.
Slings one down the leg side, Bairstow fails to clip it away.

That kept low! Morkel bowls it outside off on a good length, Bairstow looks to play from his crease. The ball does not get up at all and luckily for Jonny, it was wide of the stumps and hence he survives.
Good length around off and middle, Bairstow looks to clip it through but gets hit on his back pad.
Michael Holding spots that Philander's release of the ball is much straighter. For Olivier, the seam is angled more towards the slip cordon. Hence the swing starts early for him.
Tucks this one through mid-wicket for a single.
Nasser Hussain reckons that the change of ends has worked well for Philander since it has got the inswinger going with the wind helping him.
Better leave! Hurls a length ball outside off, Jonny covers the line and lets it go through.
Beaten! Outside off on a length, Bairstow plays for the line and hence is beaten by the away movement.
And again! Amazing consistency from the South African bowlers to follow a good ball with one on the pads. Bairstow clips it through mid-wicket and collects two runs.

JUST SHORT! Full and outside off, Bairstow looks to drive it through covers but gets an outside edge. The ball drops short of Faf du Plessis at second slip. Maybe the third slip fielder could have gone for it but there was little time and Faf went with his instincts there. Or they could just come up a touch.
Root taps it towards the off side and takes a quick single.
Deep point in place now.
Around off on a length, Bairstow looks to push but gets an inside edge onto his pads.
Slants it on the pads, tucked to fine leg for a single.
A tad short around off, Root defends it from his crease.

BEAUTY! Morkel angles one on the stumps, Root is rooted to the crease as he aims to defend it. The ball brushes the back leg and carries to de Kock. This is good bowling. They needed to bowl more of these when Root was new to the crease.
There is a deep mid-wicket in place for the mistimed pulls.
Root watches this one swing further away from him and lets it go.
Morkel bowls it outside off, Root plays inside the line and is beaten by the away movement.
Good length outside off, Bairstow looks to get it away but is beaten by the away swing.
Wide enough for Jonny to make a leave.
FOUR! As has been the case all day! Philander slants one on middle, Bairstow gets back and across and clips it through mid-wicket for a boundary.

Four Leg Byes! What happened there? Philander bowls it around off, the ball kicks off from the surface, Bairstow is hit on his back pad. The ball goes between the keeper and first slip for a boundary. Leg Byes signaled.
Fuller and outside off, Bairstow shapes to leave but the ball goes off the toe end of the bat towards the slip cordon.
In walks Jonny Bairstow at number 5. No Ben Stokes yet, remember he hurt himself on the field.

OUT! What a start for Philander! Hurls it on a length just around off, Ballance looks to force it through the off side lunging from his crease. He gets an inside edge which cannons into the stumps. Another dismissal just after the break. Nasser Hussain thinks Ballance is unlucky there, there was nothing unlucky about it. It is again the hesitancy to come fully forward which has got the better of Ballance.
A change of ends for Vernon Philander.
Good length outside off, tapped towards gully by Root. A good start for Morkel after the break.
Good length outside off, shapes away, left alone by Root.
Back of a length outside off, comes in sharply, Root looks to play at first but then lets the ball go through.
Hurls it outside off on a length, Root presses forward and defends it.
Fuller around off, Ballance wants to force it through the covers but gets an inside edge through backward square leg for a single.
Starts off with a good length ball outside off, left alone by Ballance.

The players are back out to play. South Africa will aim to begin the session well and keep the scoring in check. Joe Root and Gary Ballance will be positive, one thinks. Morne Morkel to start the proceedings. Three slips and a gully in place.
... Day 2, Session 2....

There were too many boundary balls on offer and Joe Root made them pay. He raced away to a fifty in no time. The bowlers for the tourists like their counterparts, sprayed the new ball around and did not stick to a line and length. Faf du Plessis will surely have a word and hope that they keep the scoring down and take wickets to get back on top of the game. Join us for the second session in a while.

A fantastic session of Test cricket! South Africa were wrapped up early in the day thanks to James Anderson taking a five-for. The tourists came out firing and took out the two openers in no time. It looked like they would dominate the proceedings but they lost the plot completely. The presence of a southpaw meant the South African bowlers had to adjust their lines but they failed to do so.
Floated around off stump, gets well forward and bunts it into the pitch. LUNCH ON DAY 2.
Quicker ball outside off, stays back and defends it towards cover.
Loopy and outside off, reaches out and drives it towards cover.
28th Test match fifty for Joe Root.

FOUR! No stopping Root at the moment. Flatter around middle, hangs back deep in the crease and whips it away in front of square on the leg side for a boundary. Sensational counterattack from the captain, this.
Fullish around middle, Root presses forward and blocks it down the track.
Floated on off, Ballance looks to block but gets it off the inside half towards square leg for a single.
Should be the last over before lunch. South Africa taking their time at the moment.
Time to slow the game down, Keshav Maharaj brought on for a bowl.

Michael Holding on air feels that though Olivier is getting the ball to swing, he is starting too far outside off. It is his first Test in England and that could be why he has not got his lines right. He thinks his wrist position isn't right to be bowling in these conditions. A word from his teammates would help perhaps.

FOUR! More runs but this is a good line from Olivier. Good length and zipping away from outside off, Root plays with soft hands and an angled bat. The edge results but it's still fairly in control and the ball flies between the slips and gully to the fence. Frustrating for the bowler.

TOP EDGE BUT SAFE! The short ball around off stump, good line to force a mistake and Root takes the bait with a pull. Isn't in control and miscues it over mid-wicket. The ball lands safe near the ropes as the batsmen get a brace.
Slightly fuller and just outside off, shaping away as Root makes a leave.
Full and just outside off, nicely blocked off the front foot towards cover.

FOUR! That's been clobbered! Short and on middle stump line, Root hangs back and pulls it powerfully through mid-wicket to find the fence. Another cracking shot as the runs keep coming at rapid pace for the hosts.

NOT OUT! No real surprises there. Very full and swinging in from around off, Root tries to dig it out as the ball goes back towards Olivier. It came off the boot and the Proteas are excited. The umpires aren't convinced though but go upstairs to check it. The soft signal is not out. Replays show that it did bounce before hitting the boot and then carried to the bowler.
The umpires are going upstairs for a caught and bowled appeal. The soft signal is not out. The question is regarding whether the ball bounced before hitting the boot. Let's see.
As has been the trend so far, a good ball is followed by a bad one. This is on the pads and Root clips it through mid-wicket. Won't make the fence but the batsmen take three anyway.

Play and a miss! Evidence that there is enough movement on this pitch but SA bowlers are spraying the ball around more often than not. This is on a teasing length on fourth stump line, shapes away late to beat the edge as Root hangs his bat at it.
On a length around leg stump, tucked towards square leg for a single.
Short ball this time, Ballance ducks under it just in time.

FOUR! Off the edge! This is another poor ball but Ballance still almost made a meal of it. Full and very wide outside off, he tries to reach out to it but gets a slice that flies uppishly over gully to the third man fence. Morris isn't happy with the end result but it was a boundary ball in any case.
On a good length around fourth stump line, straightens after pitching as Ballance lifts his bat to make the leave.
Length ball outside off, stays back and lets it pass to the keeper.
Good length around off stump, blocked firmly from the crease by Root.

Poor ball and punished! Story of the South African bowling so far with the new ball. They did take the two early wickets but since then, it's been an assortment of mixed lengths and lines, literally wasting the new ball. This is on the pads, clipped away through square leg for a brace.

That's a peach! This is the line he needs to be bowling consistently as he is getting enough movement. Lands it on a length around off stump, shapes away late to beat the outside edge as Root tries to push at it. Good ball!
On a length well outside off, moves further away as Root makes an easy leave.
Very full and shaping away from well outside off, Root bunts it out in time.

Michael Holding on air reckons that since Cook was stretching and playing in front of his pads, he was not in control of the shot. You normally see him being very compact. And with the conditions on offer, he reckons that he need not get that forward. Ballance is playing similarly actually.

Four Leg byes! I spoke too soon, as Morris has dished out a freebie. Strays on leg stump and although Ballance misses the flick, the ball flies off the pads past the keeper to the fine leg fence. South Africa are leaking runs with this new ball, need to be more consistent.
Visible difference in Ballance's approach today. In the first Test, he was waiting back to play deliveries late but today he has gone forward to meet them early. Has worked for him so far.
This is good from Morris, this is the zone he needs to be in. Another length ball in the corridor of uncertainty, Ballance is watchful as ever and leaves it alone.
Switches to around the wicket does Morris and gets his line right. Good length ball closer to the off stump, left alone by Ballance.
There is an issue with the sightscreen. As it is behind the crowd, the people need to be sitting quietly.
The inswinger but it's too straight from Morris, it's clipped through backward square leg for a brace.
Length ball wider outside off, easily left alone by Ballance.
On middle and leg, Ballance gets across and taps it to the leg side.
50-run stand between Root and Ballance.

FOUR! Clipped away! Root motors along. Fuller and on the pads, gets across and clips it elegantly through backward square leg. The timing is too good and the ball races to the fence for a boundary. It's been a very positive partnership for England, they have effectively wiped off the momentum SA gained with those early wickets.
Fullish and angled in closer to the off stump, tidy line as Root makes another leave.
Good movement on offer for Olivier but he needs to be a bit straighter. This is wide outside off and goes further away as Root lets it alone easily.
Nice outswinger on a fourth stump line, watchfully left alone by Root.
Fullish around middle, leans across and taps it wide of mid on for a single.
Fuller and down the leg side, Ballance tries to flick but misses as de Kock takes it well with a dive to his right.
Just short of a fuller length outside off, Root presses forward and blocks firmly to cover.
Better from Morris! Very full and on off, a bit of tail into Ballance who squirts an inside edge down to fine leg for a single.
Back of a length down the leg side, would have been a decent delivery to the right-hander but Ballance isn't one and so it's another one in the wrong line by Morris. Left alone to the keeper.
The length continues to be short outside off, spanked off the back foot to sweeper cover. Single taken.

FOUR! More runs! Short and too wide outside off, this time Root plays with an angled bat. Glides it past gully this time and the man at sweeper cover cannot get to it. Morris needs to get some discipline to succeed as this track is about doing the basics right.
Sweeper cover is in place now.

FOUR! Hammered! Morris starts with a rubbish ball, short and wide outside off stump. Root isn't going to miss out and slaps it through the covers with aplomb to find the fence. South Africa are leaking runs in the last half an hour.
Chris Morris comes on to bowl.
On a good length outside off, no shot offered by GB.

The umpires are having a word with Philander who isn't happy with the shape of the ball. It's being checked with the 8-shape gauge and handed back to the bowler. Second instance of this today after the drama before the start when Anderson had the same issue. But the ball was changed then, not now.
Fullish and on off stump, driven firmly towards mid on.

FOUR! That's sneaked through! Flurry of boundaries at the moment. Full and just outside off, Ballance gets forward to push at it with an angled bat. Plays with soft hands and the edge flies just past gully for a boundary. Morris was the man at gully and he could have done better perhaps.
Lands this on a good length on fourth stump line, nicely left alone by Ballance in response.
On a good length around off stump, Ballance defends well from the crease towards short cover.
Back of a length around middle, Root gets back and across to clip it towards deep backward square leg. Single taken.

20 runs have come in the last two overs. South Africa leaking runs at the moment. Both Root and Ballance have been positive, helped by some wayward bowling from South Africa. Maybe, it is due to the left-right combination at the crease.

FOUR! More runs for Ballance! This time Morkel tries to overcompensate and fires it on the pads. Easy for the southpaw who glances it fine down the leg side past the keeper to get another boundary. The last two overs have helped England to ease the early fall of wickets.

FOUR! CREAMED! Half volley outside off, in the slot and Ballance takes full toll of it. Reaches out to that one and drives sweetly through the covers. Timed beautifully and the ball races away to the fence.
Fractionally shorter and outside off, this is an easier leave for Gary.
This is good from Morkel, he loves bowling around the wicket to the left-hander. Lands this on a length on fourth stump line, holds its line after pitching as Ballance lets it pass.
Fullish and angled in on off stump, pushed gently towards the fielder at mid on.
Dug in short just outside off, Ballance arches his back and evades the bumper.

Back of a length on off stump, Root looks to work across the line but gets a soft leading edge towards Philander. He collects the ball in his followthrough and threatens to fire a throw back but the ball slips from his hands. Smiles all around.

FOUR! Graceful stuff! Slightly wide and on a shortish length, Root is in a positive mood and cashes in. Essays a cracking back foot punch through the covers. Finds the fence. He is looking in good touch.
The outswinger on off stump, Root moves forward and pushes it gently towards cover. Footwork is key to counter the movement, as is playing the ball late.
Back of a length outside off, this time Root lets it pass.

FOUR! JUST PAST GULLY! Nervy moment for Root. Plays away from the body as he tries to chase this away curler that's landed on a length. The slice flies just past the outstretched hands of a leaping Morris at gully. Races to the third man fence.

FOUR! Glorious from the captain! Not a half volley by any stretch of imagination but Root makes it into a boundary ball. Reaches out nicely to this one and caresses it on the up through covers for a boundary.

FOUR! Runs for the southpaw! Not exactly off the middle but Ballance won't mind. Fullish outside off, holds its line as he goes for the drive. The ball goes off the outer half through backward point. Runs all the way to the fence.
Fullish on middle and leg, worked towards square leg for a single.
Back of a length wider outside off, Root isn't tempted to have a go at it. The situation doesn't permit him to.
Fullish and on off stump, curling in, Root gets half forward and covers the movement well with a forward defence down the track.
Slightly fuller this time around middle, swinging in, Root gets it off the inner half towards fine leg. Good running gets them a brace.
Back of a length outside off, gets back and punches it towards cover.
Good ball! Lands it on a good length closer to the off pole, probably a hint of inward movement as Ballance leaves it well.
Just short of a good length wider outside off, that's an easy leave for Gary.
Probing stuff from Philander on a length closer to off stump, subtle away movement as Ballance lets it pass.
Back of a length around middle, easy for Root as he tucks this around the corner for a single.
Philander gets this straighter this time, on a length around off, Root plays with soft hands to tap it towards gully.
On a length wider outside off, shapes away considerably but the line is too wide to make Root play.
Short outside off, wide enough for Ballance to leave.
A tad short around off, Ballance taps it towards covers from his crease.
Lands it outside off, no shot offered by Gary.
Angles it on middle and leg, Ballance cannot clip it through and is hit on his pads.

Not a bad ball but Root is too good. Drifts it on middle, Root won't miss out and he clips it through the mid-wicket region. Philander hares after it from mid on and gets to it near the ropes. Three runs taken and Root gets off the mark.
Joe Root walks out to join his friend and flatmate at Yorkshire. England under pressure early in the innings yet again.

OUT! What a ball! Morkel from round the wicket, angles it just outside off on a good length, the ball pitches and goes away a touch. Jennings pushes at it from his crease. The ball takes the outside edge and carries through to de Kock behind the wickets. An easy catch for him and two in two for South Africa. What a brilliant start for them.
Gary Ballance comes out to bat. This will be a serious test for him.

OUT! That is a huge strike! Philander bowls it just around off on a length, Cook shapes to defend but is hit on his back leg and the ball lobs behind. The keeper takes the catch and the players come together and appeal long and hard. The umpire stays put and Faf du Plessis opts for the review immediately. Replays show there was a spike on the Ultra Edge as the ball went past the bat. It is a clean catch and that is a decision which has to be overturned. Philander does not need the short leg and he has the big wicket of the former England Test skipper.
South Africa have taken a review for an lbw against Cook. The Proteas are confident, even an inside edge wouldn't matter as de Kock had taken it.
Good length outside off, Cook angles it towards gully from his crease.
Shane Warne wants South Africa to have a short leg for Cook as Philander is bowling really well.
Full and outside off, Cook is forward in defence. The ball goes off the inside half towards the leg side.
And again! Hurls it just around off, Cook looks to push at it but gets another inside edge onto the pads. Philander has his hands on his head.
Length ball outside off, Cook thinks about playing but then pulls out of the shot at the last moment.

CLOSE! Fuller around off, Cook prods forward to defend but gets an inside edge onto his pads. Philander cannot reach it. There is no short leg. That was a genuine chance. Vernon has hit his straps right away.
Back of a length outside off, Jennings stays back and punches it towards point.
Short and outside off, Jennings is never going to play that.
Stays back and pushes this length ball towards covers from his crease. Morkel got good away swing there. Keaton though is happy to stay back.
Good length around off, Jennings comes forward and defends it watchfully.
Fuller around off, swings in a touch, Jennings drives it back to the bowler from his crease. That looked pleasing to the eyes.
Slants it outside off on a length, Jennings lets it to go through.
Full outside off, Cook comes nicely forward to drive it towards extra cover. Philander won't mind Cook coming forward like this.
Drifts it on the pads, clipped through the gap between mid on and mid-wicket. Maharaj gets to it first and fires the throw. Two runs taken.
Wide outside off, Cook has an easy leave.
Pushes it further outside off, brings Cook forward who taps it towards covers.
Shane Warne on air talks about working over Alastair Cook like Ryan Harris did, bowling at the off stump and getting little movement. Philander can do that really well.
Full outside off, Cook comes forward and defends it from his crease.
Bowls it outside off on a length, Cook let's it go through.
Vernon Philander to bowl from the other end. He should do well on this wicket, in these conditions.
Slants across a length ball outside off, no shot offered by Jennings.
Good length just around off, Jennings stays back and lets the ball hit his bat and the ball dies down towards the off side.
Back of a length on the body, Cook fends it through square leg for a single to get off the mark.
Hurls it outside off on a good length, Cook raises his bat and lets it go through.
What happened there? Morkel bowls it around the pads, Cook gets across to clip but fails to connect. The ball goes off something to the keeper. No appeal though. Must have been the pads.
On a good length around middle and leg, Cook turns it towards the leg side.
